service: SASSA - South African Social Security Agency
overview: SASSA administers social grants to eligible South African citizens, permanent residents, and refugees. It is the primary social safety net for millions of South Africans.

grants.name: Social Relief of Distress (SRD) Grant / R370 Grant
eligibility: South African citizen, permanent resident, or refugee
Between 18 and 60 years old
Unemployed and not receiving any other social grant or UIF
Monthly income below R625
Not a full-time student at a government-funded institution
Not resident in a government-funded institution
how_to_apply: Apply online at srd.sassa.gov.za
You need your South African ID number
Provide a cellphone number for communication
Provide banking details or select a cash collection point
Application is reviewed monthly — you must reapply or confirm every month
common_rejection_reasons: Income above R625 per month detected via bank account checks
Receiving another grant (e.g., child support grant counted as income)
Database shows employment (even if you were recently retrenched)
appeal_process: You can appeal within 90 days of the rejection decision
Appeal online at srd.sassa.gov.za under 'Appeal' section
You will need to provide supporting documents proving your eligibility
Appeals are reviewed by an independent tribunal
If your appeal is rejected, you can approach the Independent Tribunal for Social Assistance Appeals (ITSAA)
As a last resort, you can approach the High Court for judicial review

escalation.body: Independent Tribunal for Social Assistance Appeals (ITSAA)
escalation.ombudsman: If SASSA fails to process your appeal within 90 days, you may approach the Public Protector

grants.name: Child Support Grant
eligibility: Primary caregiver of a child under 18
South African citizen, permanent resident, or refugee
Caregiver income must be below R5,600 per month (single) or R11,200 combined (married)
Child must not be in a government-funded institution
Both caregiver and child must reside in South Africa
how_to_apply: Visit your nearest SASSA office in person
Bring your ID (or certified copy), child's birth certificate, proof of income
If unemployed, bring a sworn affidavit confirming unemployment
SASSA will process within 30 days (by law)
common_problems: Grant suspended without notification — usually due to child turning 18 or income change detected
Payment not received on expected date — check with SASSA or your bank
Someone else claiming the grant for your child — report fraud to SASSA

escalation.timeframe: SASSA must process applications within 30 days per Regulation 10(2)

grants.name: Older Persons Grant (Old Age Pension)
grants.amount: R2,180 per month (under 75) / R2,200 per month (75 and older) (2024/2025)
eligibility: South African citizen, permanent resident, or refugee
Women: 60 years or older / Men: 60 years or older
Income below R7,710 per month (single) or R15,420 combined (married)
Assets below R1,372,800 (single) or R2,745,600 (married)
Not maintained in a state institution
how_to_apply: Visit your nearest SASSA office
Bring your ID, proof of residence, bank statements (3 months)
If married, bring spouse's ID and income proof
Processing takes up to 30 days

grants.name: Disability Grant
eligibility: South African citizen, permanent resident, or refugee
Between 18 and 59 years old
Must have a disability that prevents you from working
Must be assessed by a SASSA-appointed medical officer
Income below R7,710 per month (single) or R15,420 combined (married)
how_to_apply: Visit your nearest SASSA office
Complete the application form and book a medical assessment
Bring your ID, medical records, proof of income
The medical assessment is free — do not pay anyone
Grant can be temporary (6-12 months) or permanent depending on the condition
common_problems: Temporary disability grant expiring — reapply before the expiry date
Medical assessment outcome disputed — request a review or second assessment
Grant stopped unexpectedly — contact SASSA immediately with reference number

grants.name: Foster Child Grant
eligibility: You must have a valid court order placing the child in your care
The child must be under 18
You must be a South African citizen, permanent resident, or refugee
how_to_apply: First obtain a foster care court order from the Children's Court
Then visit SASSA with the court order, your ID, and the child's birth certificate
SASSA processes within 30 days

grants.name: Care Dependency Grant
eligibility: Parent or caregiver of a child under 18 with a severe disability
Child requires permanent home care
Income below R5,600 per month (single) or R11,200 combined

grants.name: Grant-in-Aid
eligibility: Already receiving an Older Persons, Disability, or War Veterans grant
Require regular attendance by another person due to physical or mental condition

your_rights: Section 27(1)(c) of the Constitution of South Africa guarantees the right to social security
SASSA must process applications within 30 days (Regulation 10(2) of the Social Assistance Act)
You have the right to appeal any decision within 90 days
SASSA must give you written reasons for any rejection
You may not be asked to pay any fees for a SASSA application — it is always free
If SASSA fails to pay your grant on time, they must provide back-pay for the missed months
You have the right to receive your grant at a pay point of your choice
